verifications.claim: According to Freddie Mac and Mortgage News Daily, as of late March 2026, average 30-year fixed mortgage rates have risen to approximately 6.38%–6.64%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Freddie Mac 30 Year Fixed (weekly) Mar 26 2026 3/26/26 6.38%', 'MND's 30 Year Fixed ... Mar 27 2026 3/27/26 6.64%'; R7: 'average rate on a 30-year fixed home loan surged to 6.38% for the week ending March 26, according to Freddie Mac'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches Freddie Mac 6.38% (week ending 3/26) and MND highs around 6.64% (3/27) in late March, with rise noted.

verifications.claim: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rates are up from previous weeks
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources show weekly and daily increases in late March.

verifications.claim: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rates remain lower than early 2025 levels
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: YOY changes negative e.g. '6.64% ... YOY -0.18%'; R7: 'rates are lower than the same time in 2025, when mortgage interest rates averaged 6.65%'; R10: 'below the 7% levels seen in early 2025'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm current rates lower than 2025 equivalents.

verifications.claim: As of late March 2026, 15-year fixed rates are averaging around 5.87%–5.97%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to range on March 29 (late March); minor variance in lower bound but closely aligns.

verifications.claim: As of March 27-30, 2026, 30-year fixed mortgage rates are 6.38% to 6.64%
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.reasoning: For exact dates 27-30, MND rates 6.55%-6.64%; 6.38% is Freddie Mac week ending 3/26, not those days—lower bound mismatches specific dates.

verifications.claim: As of March 27-30, 2026, 15-year fixed mortgage rates are 5.87% to 5.97%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches range on March 29 within specified dates.

verifications.claim: As of March 27-30, 2026, 5/1 ARM mortgage rates are 5.87% to 6.87%
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.reasoning: Upper end matches, but lower 5.87% not supported for 5/1 ARM (5.53% is VA, not standard ARM); range lower bound incorrect.

verifications.claim: Rising tensions in the Middle East have influenced oil prices
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'Iran conflict pushes up oil prices'; 'war in Iran has put further pressure on inflation'
verifications.reasoning: Direct link between Middle East (Iran) tensions and rising oil prices.

verifications.claim: Rising tensions in the Middle East have caused market volatility
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'war in Iraq, which has rattled financial markets, has led to interest rate volatility'; R10: 'Iran conflict ... roiled energy markets'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly connect Middle East war/tensions to market rattling and volatility.

verifications.claim: Rising tensions in the Middle East have pushed mortgage rates up
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R7: 'war in Iraq ... led to interest rate volatility'; R10: 'rates increased sharply just as ... Iran roiled energy markets ... rising oil prices'
verifications.reasoning: Indirect via oil/inflation/market volatility; no direct statement that tensions pushed mortgage rates up.

verifications.claim: Increased inflation has reduced expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'increasing inflation has renewed the possibility of Federal Reserve rate increases rather than rate cuts'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports reduced expectations for cuts due to inflation.

verifications.claim: Increased inflation has contributed to higher mortgage rates
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Inflation: Rising inflation ... prompting lenders to increase mortgage rates'; R10: 'inflation is on the rise ... mortgage rates jump'

verifications.claim: Increasing housing inventory is providing more options for buyers
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'Homebuyers have more options as the number of homes for sale has exceeded 2025 levels'; 'Home listing options for buyers'

verifications.claim: According to Freddie Mac and Mortgage News Daily, inflationary pressures and geopolitical tensions drove average 30-year fixed mortgage rates higher as of late March 2026
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6/R7: Report rates (6.38%-6.64%) and rises but no mention of causes like inflation or geopolitical tensions attributed to them
verifications.reasoning: Rates and rise supported, but drivers (inflation, tensions) not stated by Freddie Mac/MND; falsely attributed.
